ازاي أحل مسائل ال equilibrium و ال not equilibrium ؟!

أول حاجه قاعدة مهمه كده ان دائما قانون ال p+ q = 1

طب ليه و ايه العلاقة ؟ 
لان القانون ده أصلًا حاصل ضرب القوسين اللي هم قانون ال ( p+q = 1 )  و دي حاجه كنا واخدينها في الرياضة زمان
 # و ده مش في حالة ال equilibrium بس ده في أي حالة حرفيًا 
طب إزاي

كذلك ال alleles انا مهما عملت عندي 100% من ال alleles ياما A ياما a مهما زادوا أو قلوا 

طب انا اصلا يستخدم القوانين دي ليه ؟
ببساطه عشان دي طريقة بجيب بيها ال genotype frequency اللي هم P, H, Q بالقانون الطويل ده و عشان اجيب ال allele frequency من القانون التاني اللي هو p+q = 1

طب و ليه مجيبش ال p مش ال q ؟! 
افضل تجيب ال q و دي اللي بنثبتها عموما )

اشمعنا 6.25 ؟! 
لان كل 100 جرام بروتين فيه 16 نيتروجين 
فهنقسم ال 100/16=6.25

العملية دي كلها بتتم على أربع خطوات بطريقة ال Kjeldahl method 

1. Digestion: 

هنا الهدف كله اني ادخل النيتروجين في مركب solid عشان أبدأ أول مراحل الفصل عن باقي المكونات 

بجيب حاجه اسمها digestion tube مقاسها 250ml بحط فيها 1gm dry sample + catalyst ( 0.7gm copper sulphate & 10 gm potassium sulphate) 
+ 25ml of concentrated sulfuric acid 
و بعدين بحط الأنبوبة دي في جهاز اسمه ال digester ده بينهم الحرارة على خطوتين 
الأولى : gentle heating  عشان ميفورش في الأول 
التانية : vigorous boiling at 420 Celsius لمدة 3-4hr 
النتيجة إن ال solution اللي هيطلع هيبقى شفاف تمامًا و معاه  
 ammonium salts و بعض الشوائب الأخرى فهحتاج أفصل تاني النيتروجين أكتر عشان اقيسه فتدخل على الخطوة التانية 

Distillation : 

أول حاجه بضيف 200ml distilled water+ 100ml sodium hydroxide ( NaOH) + pumice stone or zinc granules ده عشان الأنبوبة متفرقعش أثناء التفاعل 
كده بقا ال nitrogen هيتفاعل مع ال NaOH و يطلع لي ammonia gas ( NH3 ) 
لكده فصلته عن كل الشوائب و بقا gas بس لسه فاضلي خطوة اني احجمه و أقيسه 
فلازم اعمل condensation في أنابيب تدخل على beaker فيها 50ml N/10 sulfuric acid ( H2SO4 ) + methyl red indicator 
عشان ترجع تتفاعل معاه أتاني مرة بس المرة دي من غير أي شوائب 
طب اشمعنا 50 ml ?! 
دي كمية أكبر من اللي النيتروجين هيحتاجها أكيد و ده الشرط الأساسي عشان نعرف أحسب منها فهلجأ لخطوة ال titration  

3. Titration: 

احنا قولنا في جزء من ال sulfuric acid لسه free مش متفاعل مع حاجه باقي من ال 50ml فهمله titration باني اضيف NaOH ( لتاني مرة في التجربة ) و افضل ازود لحد ما ال methyl red indicator يغير اللون فاقفل بسرعة و مضيفش اكتر عشان الحسابات تطلع مظبوطه لاني هقيس كمية ال NaOH اللي اتضافت بالظبط 

كده حجمنا اللي كان gas في تفاعل فاضل أقيسه فهشوف كمية الNaOH اللي اتعمل بيها titration من السحاحة و نحسب من خلالها كمية ال H2SO4 اللي كانت free و بناءً عليه اطرح يطلع اللي التفاعل مع النيتروجين بالظبط  و كده يبقا ناقصني بس الحسابات 

4. Calculations : 

1ml of N/ 10 H2SO4: 0.0014 gm of nitrogen 
Weight of nitrogen= Volume of N/10 H2SO4* 0.0014
كده جبنا الوزن بتاع النيتروجين بس انا في القانون بتاع ال CP محتاج ال nitrogen % 
Nitrogen % = ( weight of N/ weight of sample) * 100 

و كده أقدر أطبق القانون الأولاني خالص 

CP = N% * 6.25

Animal Nutrition & Feed Definitions
 * Nutrition: The process by which an organism absorbs or utilizes food, including water and minerals.
 * Rations: A 24-hour total allowance of feed given to an animal.
 * Feeding Stuff: Any material containing nutritional value.
 * Nutrients: Substances that aid in supporting animal life and bodily functions.
 * Digestible Nutrients (DN): Digestible Nutrients = Nutrient Content - Nutrient in Feces
 * Digestion Coefficient (DC): DC = (Digestible Nutrient / Nutrient in Feed) * 100
 * True Digestibility: True Digestibility = [(Nutrient in Feed - (Nutrient in Feces - Metabolic Fecal Loss)) / Nutrient in Feed] * 100
 * Total Digestible Nutrients (TDN): TDN = DP + DC + (DEE * 2.25)
 * Basal Feed:
   * Primary source of energy.
   * Protein content: 10–14%.
   * Fat content: Less than 5%.
   * Main components: Starches and sugars.
 * Supplements:
   * Used to improve the nutritive balance.
   * Contain large amounts of Protein.
   * Single feed supplements contain 20% or more Protein.
 * Concentrates vs. Roughages:
   * Concentrates:
     * Feed containing large amounts of nutrients in small amounts of feed.
     * Supplies primary nutrients (Protein, Carbohydrate, and Fat).
     * Contains less than 18% Crude Fiber (CF).
   * Roughage:
     * Feed containing small amounts of nutrients in large amounts of feed.
     * High in fiber content (more than 18% Crude Fiber).
     * Utilized by ruminants, horses, and rabbits via microflora digestion.
 * Types of Rations:
   * Balanced Ration: Contains all required nutrients based on National Research Council (NRC) recommendations.
   * Maintenance Ration: Formulated for animals doing no work and producing no yield, ensuring neither weight gain nor loss.
Part 2: Nutritive Ratio & Chemical Composition
 * Nutritive Ratio (NR):
   * Formula: NR = DCP : (DCH + DEE * 2.25) OR (TDN - DCP) / DCP
   * Narrow NR (1:6 or less): Higher Protein content, Less Energy.
   * Medium NR (1:7).
   * Wide NR (1:8 or higher): Lower Protein content, Higher Energy.
 * Composition of Food:
   * Food: Water + Dry Matter
   * Dry Matter: Inorganic (Minerals) + Organic (Carbohydrates, Lipids, Proteins, Vitamins)
 * Water & Fat Content in Animal Body:
   * Water percentage decreases as age increases.
   * In cattle:
     * Embryo: 95% Water.
     * At birth: 75–80% Water.
     * At 5 months: 66–72% Water.
     * Mature: 50–60% Water.
   * Inverse relationship: As Fat increases, Water decreases.
   * Very fat animals have around 40% Water.
   * Total Water + Fat = 75–80%.
   * Protein is the second most abundant component after water.
 * Carbohydrates & Vitamins in Animals:
   * Carbohydrates: Represent less than 1% of body weight (e.g., Glucose in blood, Glycogen in muscle and liver).
   * Vitamins: Present in minute amounts; essential components of enzyme systems.
 * Composition in Plants:
   * Water decreases as plant age increases.
   * Carbohydrates increase with plant maturation.
   * Protein moves from leaves to seeds as the plant matures.

By: Retag Hossam

⛔short note on lec 3 Anatomy.

 1️⃣Briefly explain the structural and functional differences between sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers regarding their pre- and post-ganglionic lengths and origins.  
​
⭕​Origin: The sympathetic system originates from the thoracolumbar region of the spinal cord, whereas the parasympathetic system originates from the craniosacral region (including cranial nerves III, VII, IX, X, and sacral nerves).  
⭕​Fiber Length: In the sympathetic system, preganglionic fibers are short while postganglionic fibers are long. Conversely, in the parasympathetic system, the arrangement is the exact vice versa (long preganglionic and short postganglionic fibers).  

2️⃣Write a short note on the origin, pathway, and termination of the Vagus nerve.  
​
⭕​Origin: It originates from the lateral aspect of the medulla oblongata and exits the cranium through the jugular foramen.  
⭕​Pathway: In the neck, it joins the sympathetic trunk to form the vagosympathetic trunk. The dorsal and ventral branches of both left and right vagus nerves unite on the esophagus to form the dorsal and ventral vagal trunks, which enter the abdominal cavity through the esophageal hiatus.  
⭕​Termination: The dorsal vagal trunk ends in the celiacomesenteric ganglia and the visceral surface of the stomach, while the ventral vagal trunk ramifies on the parietal surface of the stomach.  

3️⃣Write a short note on the formation and function of the brachial plexus. 
 
​ ⭕The brachial plexus is formed by the ventral branches of cervical and thoracic spinal nerves (C6 + C7 + C8 + Th1 + Th2 in equines). Its main function is to supply the forelimb with motor and sensory innervation.
